title: Hydra-Nav: Object Navigation via Adaptive Dual-Process Reasoning
claim: A single unified model adaptively alternates between a slow reasoning mode and a fast action mode, updating its memory when it switches.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right token sequence, memory-update inset at right
description: A wide single-panel diagram of the architecture. A central rounded blue box labeled 'Hydra-Nav' sits between two rows of token blocks. The top row is the input: blue instruction tokens ('Find a TV.'), orange long-term-memory image tokens, and yellow current-view tokens. The bottom row is the output: gray dashed tokens, a red reasoning token and green low-level action tokens. Indoor photos sit above the input tokens. Brackets and arrows mark a red 'Slow system' region and a green 'Fast system' region. A dashed arrow across the top is labeled 'Switch & Clear context'. A red text bubble at bottom left shows example reasoning, and green arrows show TurnLeft and MoveAhead actions. At right, an 'Obs' token triggers a panoramic scan. The scan images are added to the full context. They then produce a new landmark text entry in the orange long-term-memory box. Color coding separates the token types, and the eye goes first to the central Hydra-Nav box.
caption: The architecture of Hydra-Nav. Hydra-Nav receives user instruction, long-term memory, and previous image-action pairs, then outputs reasoning (optionally) and meta-actions. Hydra-Nav adaptively switches between the fast and slow systems by outputting the special transition token obs. Specifically, the panoramic scan triggered by obs is extracted as a new landmark and inserted into the existing long-term memory.
abstract: While large vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for object goal navigation, current methods still struggle with low success rates and inefficient localization of unseen objects--failures primarily attributed to weak temporal-spatial reasoning. Meanwhile, recent attempts to inject reasoning into VLM-based agents improve success rates but incur substantial computational overhead. To address both the ineffectiveness and inefficiency of existing approaches, we introduce Hydra-Nav, a unified VLM architecture that adaptively switches between a deliberative slow system for analyzing exploration history and formulating high-level plans, and a reactive fast system for efficient execution. We train Hydra-Nav through a three-stage curriculum: (i) spatial-action alignment to strengthen trajectory planning, (ii) memory-reasoning integration to enhance temporal-spatial reasoning over long-horizon exploration, and (iii) iterative rejection fine-tuning to enable selective reasoning at critical decision points. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Hydra-Nav achieves state-of-the-art performance on the HM3D, MP3D, and OVON benchmarks, outperforming the second-best methods by 11.1%, 17.4%, and 21.2%, respectively. Furthermore, we introduce SOT (Success weighted by Operation Time), a new metric to measure search efficiency across VLMs with varying reasoning intensity. Results show that adaptive reasoning significantly enhances search efficiency over fixed-frequency baselines.
